newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nomura denies president to resign.
newsitem.headline: Nomura denies president to resign.

text.p: A Nomura Securities Co Ltd spokesman on Friday denied that Nomura president Hideo Sakamaki would resign to take responsibility for the involvement of two of the brokerage's directors in apparently irregular deals with a corporate client.
"That is not being considered at all," the spokesman said.

Nomura vice president Atsushi Saito said on Thursday that Japan's securities watchdog was investigating stock transactions which he said the two directors made through the client's accut approval of the client.

Saito also said on Thursday that the two directors appeared to have transferred profits from Nomura's own funds to the customer's account. Asked if the client was a "sokaiya", or a firm involved in corporate racketeering, Saito said he could not confirm that at the moment.
Kyodo news service, quoting "financial sources", said on Friday that Sakamaki was likely to step down soon over the incident.

Kyodo also reported, quoting the same sources, that Japan's securities watchdog, the Securities and Exchange Surveillance Commission (SESC), may file a complaint with the Tokyo District Public Prosecutor's Office.
The SESC was not immediately available for comment on the Kyodo report.
